title: Two lanthanide-hydroxo clusters with different nuclearity: Synthesis, structures, luminescent and magnetic properties

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.compound_name: pentanuclear terbium(III) hydroxo cluster with dibenzoylmethanate

synthesis.procedure: A solution of TbCl3·6H2O (0.2 mmol, 74 mg) in 10 mL cold water was added slowly with stirring to a solution of Hdbm (0.6 mmol, 135 mg) in 45 mL 95% ethanol. Aqueous NH3·H2O (1.0 M) was added to keep pH 7.0–7.5, giving yellow precipitates. Stirring was continued for about 30 min; the precipitates were filtered, washed with water and air-dried (78% yield based on TbCl3·6H2O). Block pale yellow crystals of 1 were obtained by recrystallization in CH2Cl2/n-C6H14 (1:1, 10 mL).
synthesis.temperature: cold water for the metal-salt solution; otherwise not specified (ambient implied)
synthesis.vessel_or_method: aqueous/ethanolic precipitation followed by recrystallization from mixed solvents
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Yellow precipitates filtered, washed with water and air-dried; block pale yellow crystals obtained by recrystallization in CH2Cl2/n-C6H14 (1:1, 10 mL).

properties.summary: No detectable Tb(III) emission in the solid state because the Hdbm triplet–5D4 gap (~70 cm−1) is too small for sensitization. χMT at 300 K is 58.59 cm3 K mol−1 (close to 59.1 for five isolated Tb(III)); it decreases slowly to ~70 K then drops to 25.36 cm3 K mol−1 at 1.8 K, attributed to Stark-level depopulation and weak antiferromagnetic coupling. AC susceptibility (100 Oe dc, 1.0 Oe ac, 1–1488 Hz) shows no peaks or frequency dependence, so 1 is not an SMM.

measurements.name: ac susceptibility / SMM test
measurements.value: no frequency-dependent χ′ or χ″ peaks
measurements.conditions: 100 Oe dc field, 1.0 Oe oscillating field, 1–1488 Hz

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.compound_name: tetranuclear samarium(III) hydroxo cluster with dibenzoylmethanate

synthesis.procedure: Prepared by the same procedure as 1, replacing TbCl3·6H2O with SmCl3·6H2O (0.2 mmol, 73 mg). Yellow solids obtained in 72% yield (based on SmCl3·6H2O). Block yellow crystals of 2 obtained by the same CH2Cl2/n-C6H14 recrystallization as 1.
synthesis.temperature: same as 1 (cold water for metal-salt solution; otherwise not specified)
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Yellow solids isolated; block yellow crystals obtained by recrystallization in CH2Cl2/n-C6H14 as for 1.

properties.summary: Solid-state excitation at 405 nm gives characteristic Sm(III) visible emission at ~565, 605 and 647 nm (4G5/2 → 6H5/2, 6H7/2, 6H9/2), with orange emission dominated by 565 nm and Stark splitting of 6H7/2 at 600 and 608 nm. χMT at 300 K is 1.31 cm3 K mol−1 (larger than 0.36 expected for four ground-state Sm(III) ions because excited 6HJ levels are populated) and falls monotonically to 0.05 cm3 K mol−1 at 1.8 K from thermal depopulation of excited levels.

measurements.name: excitation wavelength
measurements.conditions: solid state, room temperature (maximum of excitation spectrum)
